solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On-line delivery service

parts.note: not an internet service: something that delivers goods while running along a railway line

explanation.surface: An internet business that brings parcels to your door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' suggests the internet, but the line here is a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: A goods train runs on rails and delivers cargo, so it is literally a delivery service on a line.

clue.text: Loud, not just where the roundabouts are

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud
something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: A complaint that noisy traffic junctions are unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundabouts are road junctions in the surface, but here they are merry-go-round rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundabouts, the British word for merry-go-rounds, are found at a travelling fairground.

clue.text: Wise to be navigating initially in lake?

indicators.note: in places the picked letter within the lake's name

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word navigating

explanation.surface: Is it sensible to go sailing on a lake?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' looks like an adjective, but it is Ernie Wise, of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, so his surname leads to his first name.

clue.text: Joy sends lag crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wildly disordered, so the letters of the two words get mixed up

explanation.surface: A convict is driven mad with happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges SENDS LAG; a lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy and the answer are synonyms, both naming a feeling of great happiness.

clue.text: Writes about losing one item of clothing

indicators.note: about signals that the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
losing tells us a letter drops out of the word Writes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone composes text about losing a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing one' drops I from WRITES to leave WRTES, which 'about' rearranges. Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are tartan trousers, a Scottish garment, so they are one article of dress.

clue.text: Part perfect trendsetter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
a model pupil or husband is a perfect one

explanation.surface: An actor who plays a part flawlessly sets the fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A person others copy and look up to sets the standard, as a trendsetter does.

clue.text: Spike, masculine friend that is going round

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the first letters are placed around the others

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A list describing a man and his mate walking around a spike.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike something is to pierce it on a point, which is the verb's meaning here.

clue.text: Posh fellows in crime, packing

indicators.note: in places the posh fellows within the crime

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a kind of crime
U is the British shorthand for upper-class, posh
FF is an abbreviation of fellows, the plural of F

explanation.surface: Upper-class men involved in a criminal act that involves packing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing is material used for packing cushions or poultry, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Double order for tea dance

indicators.note: double means the piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea, as asked for in an order

explanation.surface: Asking for two cups at a tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea dance is an afternoon dance with tea; here 'tea' becomes CHA, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance, so it is one example of a dance.

clue.text: Peerless example of wrought iron panel

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine sample of a panel of worked iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought iron' looks like a single phrase; 'wrought' is the anagram signal working on IRON PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a person or thing without equal, a peerless example.

clue.text: Piece of ground where tap is situated in front of church

indicators.note: in front of puts the first piece before the next one

parts.note: to pat is to tap gently

explanation.surface: Describing a plot where a water tap stands before a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tap' is a water fitting in the surface but a light stroke in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A small plot of land, such as a vegetable plot, is called a patch.

clue.text: Declare sun's over infernal regions

parts.note: to aver is to declare firmly

indicators.note: over signals that the word for the star is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: the 's is just 'is', so this gives the plain word sun

explanation.surface: Announcing that the sun has set over the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Avernus, a lake in Italy thought to be the entrance to Hades, stands for the underworld itself.

clue.text: Man providing backing caught doing mischief

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the conditional word is read backwards

parts.note: providing means if, as in a condition
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A man supporting someone is caught misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefic means causing harm or evil, so it describes something doing mischief.

clue.text: Dependable Dirk cools off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reliable Dirk calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cools off' reads as a phrase; 'off' is the anagram signal on DIRK COOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely firm and stable can be relied upon, so it is dependable.

clue.text: Angry lawyers may get support

parts.note: cross means angry
the Bar is the collective term for barristers

explanation.surface: Angry lawyers may receive backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbar is a horizontal beam that holds a structure up, a kind of support.

clue.text: Warren's bra thinly disguised!

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is warren

indicators.note: disguised means changed in appearance, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Warren wears a flimsy bra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warren' reads as a person's name, but it is a maze of burrows, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a network of tunnels, and a maze of passages is a labyrinth.

clue.text: Advisable to include endorsement

indicators.note: to include says the word holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: It is wise to add an endorsement.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement stamped in a passport allowing entry.

clue.text: In poor shape but not when on course

definitions.meaning: unwell or performing below normal standard
on a golf course, a score under the standard is good, not poor

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means below normal health, yet in golf scoring below standard is a success.

clue.text: Penny cut off sound

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A coin is snipped off with a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A plop is the sound of something small dropping into water.

clue.text: One in political group achieving equal status

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the group

parts.note: a party is a political group
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A member of a political party gains equality.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity means equality, especially equality of standing or value.

clue.text: Dog trapping naughty lad's bird

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the dog surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the boy's letters get mixed up

parts.note: the 's is not a letter, so this gives lad

explanation.surface: A dog catches a bad boy's bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' sits at the end as the definition, while 'naughty' scrambles the boy into ALD for the dog to trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is a large North American bird of prey.

clue.text: Was no longer an outsider

parts.note: someone who stepped from outside to inside a place stopped being outside it

explanation.surface: Someone finally became accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests social acceptance; literally it just means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in through a door means one stops being outside, so the verb fits literally.

clue.text: Sportsman, amateur, coming into the fold with hesitant expression

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so the abbreviation goes inside the fold

parts.note: a ply is a fold or layer
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An amateur sportsman joins the team, uncertainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who takes part in a sport or game.

clue.text: Dishonest stocktaker

parts.note: not a crooked shop auditor: someone who unlawfully takes livestock

explanation.surface: A fraudulent auditor counting goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock means livestock here, and taking means stealing, not counting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, literally taking stock dishonestly.

clue.text: Returned rifle with Christopher's instrument set

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for plunder is read backwards

parts.note: to rifle a place is to loot it
Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: A gun is given back along with Christopher's set of tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun, but it is the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instruments or implements kept together is a kit of tools.

clue.text: Paul's companion seen in America following bird

indicators.note: following puts the country after the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A friend of Paul is spotted in the USA after a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a companion of the apostle Paul and receives one of his New Testament letters.

clue.text: King has a set not working

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A king's device has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is informal for broken, so it means not functioning.

clue.text: Flatterer finds plaything enthralling these days

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the toy holds the other letters

parts.note: a toy is a plaything
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A sycophant is captivated by a modern toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady fawns over others, so a flatterer or sycophant is one.

clue.text: Way of sending messages when Peter Pan flies round globe

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the anagram goes around the ring
flies means moves wildly, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a globe is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Peter Pan flies around the world sending news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' rearranges PETER PAN, and 'round' wraps that around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper for writing letters on is a medium by which messages are sent.

clue.text: Arranged for gold casket getting evaluated

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a casket is a small chest
rated means evaluated

explanation.surface: Gold box being valued for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate something is to arrange or organise it, as music is arranged for an orchestra.
